title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Desk Guide: Earnings Disregard Share for Attached Workers on a Supplemental Correction
content:
For a supplemental correction on an Unemployment Benefit Claims record, the disregard share — the share of the weekly benefit amount that sets the earnings disregard of the corrected week, rounded to the cent — follows the claimant's recent work attachment and approved training.

**Attachment hours** are the hours on every certification of the claim whose week ended within the three calendar months before the handling date, added together.

| Approved training on the claim | Attachment hours | Disregard share |
|---|---|---|
| Enrolled | At least 100 | 0.5 (the attached-training share) |
| Not enrolled | At least 100 | 0.4 (the attached-worker share) |
| Either | Fewer than 100 | The program's disregard share |

Any other supplemental correction uses the program's disregard share.

## Points of judgement

- The 100-hour test is met at exactly 100.0 hours; 99.5 hours does not meet it.
- A certification whose week ended more than three calendar months before the handling date contributes no hours.
- Approved training counts only when the claim records it as enrolled.

### Hypothetical figure

A claimant enrolled in approved training, with 104.0 attachment hours and a weekly benefit amount of 346.00, has a disregard of 0.5 times 346.00, that is 173.00; without training the disregard would be 0.4 times 346.00, that is 138.40.
